findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch on every cron run
findings.body:
One `try` wraps the entire `for` loop of `client.request` calls, and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises run only at the end via `Promise.all`. Prisma promises are lazy, so if any cancel request throws, the loop stops and none of the queued deletes execute.

This includes reminders that SendGrid already cancelled earlier in the same run. They keep `cancelled: true`, so the next run re-POSTs a cancel for those batch ids. SendGrid can reject a cancel for a batch that is already cancelled, and that failure aborts the loop again.

Concrete triggers:
- the 100 pending-cancellation limit;
- a batch already cancelled through the `immediateDelete` path (e.g. organizer `requestReschedule` sets `cancelled=true`, then the attendee reschedules and `handleNewBooking` cancels the same batch immediately);
- a null `referenceId`.

One bad row therefore blocks every other cancellation until its `scheduledDate` passes, and those other emails are sent. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete or mark each row right after its own request succeeds.

findings.title: Reschedule still uses immediate SendGrid cancel and leaves the reminder row behind
findings.body:
For rescheduled bookings, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` POSTs to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` immediately. That is the exact behaviour the PR identifies as broken: it consumes SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation quota, and once the quota is full these cancels fail and rescheduled-booking reminders are still sent.

The `immediateDelete` branch in `emailReminderManager.ts` also returns without deleting the row or marking it cancelled. The row stays with `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`. If it was already `cancelled: true` (from `requestReschedule`), or is later marked cancelled by a workflow edit, the cron sends a second cancel for the same batch.

The old booking is not deleted here, so the deferred path (no `immediateDelete`) works and should be used. Otherwise the immediate path should at least delete the row.

findings.title: Workflow/step deletion still cancels immediately and is subject to the 100-cancellation limit
findings.body:
When a workflow is deleted (and when a step is deleted, line 521), every scheduled email reminder is cancelled with `immediateDelete=true`. That issues one SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel per reminder right away.

A workflow active on many event types can easily have more than 100 scheduled reminders in the 72h window. Past the account-wide limit, the remaining cancels fail. The failures are only logged inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, and the rows are then cascade-deleted with the workflow or step, so nothing retries. Those reminders are still delivered after the user deleted the workflow.

This path needs its own deferred mechanism, for example detaching or keeping cancelled rows instead of cascade-deleting them before the cron processes them.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation DB writes are fire-and-forget (previously awaited)
findings.body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are called inside `forEach` without being awaited or added to `prismaPromises`. Before this PR, the `workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises were awaited.

Now the handler can return before the `cancelled: true` update, the row delete or the Twilio cancel completes. In serverless deployments, work after the response may be frozen or dropped. The flag is then never set, the cron never cancels the email, and the reminder for the cancelled booking is sent: the bug this PR is meant to fix.

The same pattern appears in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule` (line 490), `handleNewBooking.ts`, and the `workflows.tsx` update paths. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` them.

findings.title: Deferring cancellation for imminent reminders can miss SendGrid's cancel cutoff
findings.body:
Every cancellation with a `referenceId` is now deferred to the cron by setting `cancelled: true`, whatever the reminder's `scheduledDate`. The cron runs every 15 minutes, and SendGrid only honours a scheduled-send cancel made at least ~10 minutes before send time.

If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled roughly 10–25 minutes before its reminder is due, the cron may not run before the cutoff, so the email goes out. The previous immediate cancel would have stopped it.

Cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is already inside the cron's 1-hour window; only reminders further out need to be deferred.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import after removing batch-delete code
findings.body:
`Prisma` is still imported from `@prisma/client`, but its only use was in the removed `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]` arrays, so it is now unused. The import also lost its trailing comma.

This will trip lint (no-unused-vars) and formatting checks.
